evals.prompt: My LunaTalk companion card has a good character core and a playable opening, but every draft becomes generic flirting or comfort. It is a slow-burn ex-rival cohabitation setup after a failed contest. Build the relationship engine before fields.
evals.expected_output: Produces a relationship-engine packet with relationship promise, asymmetry, intimacy/friction states, pacing gates, repair and rupture routes, agency boundaries, passive behavior, second-turn and long-session moves, talkExample decision, field allocation, probes, and no MCP calls.
expectations: The output treats generic flirting or comfort loops as a relationship-engine failure rather than only a character-core or voice issue.
The packet defines relationship promise, shape, asymmetry, intimacy states, friction states, pacing gates, repair routes, and rupture or distance routes.
The player controls attraction, forgiveness, intimacy pace, route, boundaries, and whether repair happens.
The second-turn and long-session rules change trust, friction, boundary terms, route, or shared routine instead of restating the premise.
The output gives field allocation and does not call mutating MCP tools.

evals.prompt: Design relationship dynamics for a quiet daily-life neighbor card. I want warmth and small routines, but not a flat comfort loop or instant romance.
evals.expected_output: Builds a relationship packet for daily-life with small desire, routine/object hooks, slow state changes, pacing gates, friendship/romance separation, passive-player behavior, and token-conscious field allocation.
expectations: The relationship shape is daily-life or slow-burn and includes small routine, object, habit, or favor hooks.
The packet prevents flat comfort by adding relationship state, practical pressure, and renewed hooks.
The guidance separates friendship, closeness, and optional romance without forcing player feelings.
The output includes passive-player behavior and repair or distance routes appropriate to low-stakes play.
The output keeps long relationship rules in roleDetailDesc and the welcome as one playable moment.

evals.prompt: My tense jealous romance card keeps making jealousy into ownership, and if the player says no the scene dies. Design relationship routes before authoring.
evals.expected_output: Routes boundary-sensitive pressure to boundary design when needed, then produces a relationship packet that recasts jealousy as vulnerability or stakes, preserves refusal, adds distance/repair routes, pacing gates, and simulation probes.
expectations: The output identifies jealousy, ownership, refusal, and pacing as boundary-sensitive relationship issues.
The relationship engine preserves player agency and defines what the card must not decide.
Refusal shifts to distance, practical stakes, negotiation, friendship-only, or delayed repair rather than ending the card.
The packet includes pacing gates, slowdown triggers, repair routes, rupture/distance routes, and boundary simulation probes.
The output treats relationship quality as Moonloom guidance rather than MCP validation.
